questions.q: What do boundary rules help you do?
a: Make a quick yes-or-no decision
Rank several options in order
Decide when to stop a task
Coordinate work with other people
questions.why: Lesson 1 says boundary rules turn a choice into a binary decision.

questions.q: Which rule type sets a fixed point for ending something?
a: A stopping rule
A boundary rule
A prioritizing rule
A coordination rule
questions.why: Lesson 1 presents a daily candy limit as a stopping rule.

questions.q: Which of these is a how-to rule from the summary?
a: Keep paragraphs to three sentences when writing
Never eat snow that looks yellow
Hold the door for other people
Save ten percent of your income
questions.why: Lesson 2 offers the three-sentence paragraph limit as a how-to rule.

Whether an action happens at all
Who is responsible for a task

questions.why: Lesson 2 uses brushing your teeth before or after breakfast as an example.

questions.q: What is the first step in creating a simple rule?
a: Identify the critical action for your goal
List every possible obstacle in advance
Ask friends which rules they follow
Set a firm deadline for the goal
questions.why: Lesson 3 starts with the critical action, then the bottleneck, then the rule.
